title: A New Model for the Milky Way Halo Dispersion Measure with the ENGAWA Simulations: Low DMs and Large Anisotropy
comment: 13 pages, 12 figures, 2 tables. Python package available at https://github.com/slucchini/l26halodm
summary: Fast radio burst (FRB) dispersion measures (DMs) are powerful tracers of the low density universe, but interpretation is made difficult by the integrated nature of DM. In this paper, we analyze the new ENGAWA cosmological zoom-in simulation suite to constrain the DM contribution from the Milky Way (MW) halo. The ENGAWA simulations consist of four Milky Way-like galaxies with enhanced resolution in the circumgalactic medium, making them an excellent tool to probe the properties of the gaseous halo. The median all-sky DM from the galactic halos in ENGAWA span 19-39 pc cm$^{-3}$, varying even at fixed feedback strength, halo mass, and $f_\mathrm{CGM}$. These simulations show that, with enhanced circumgalactic resolution, the mean halo DM values are in general lower with more anisotropy across the sky than previous models, reaching < 10 pc cm$^{-3}$ towards the poles. Furthermore, by varying the solar position within the simulated galaxies, we have obtained an estimate of the uncertainty in DM given our location in the MW. We provide a Python package with MW halo DM values from the simulation accessible via API functions of Galactic longitude and latitude. These new, simulation-based MW halo DM estimates will provide a critical baseline for interpretations of future FRB observations and our understanding of the global gas distribution in the Universe.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the ENGAWA cosmological zoom-in simulation suite to constrain the Milky Way halo's contribution to fast radio burst dispersion measures, finding median all-sky DMs of 19-39 pc cm⁻³ with strong sky anisotropy and lower polar values (<10 pc cm⁻³), and provides a Python package for MW halo DM estimates as a function of Galactic coordinates.
AI.motivation: FRB dispersion measures are powerful tracers of the low-density universe, but their interpretation is hindered by the integrated nature of DM, particularly the uncertain contribution from the Milky Way halo. Better constraints on the MW halo DM are needed to enable accurate cosmological interpretations of FRB observations.
AI.method: The authors use the ENGAWA cosmological zoom-in simulation suite, which consists of four Milky Way-like galaxies with enhanced resolution in the circumgalactic medium. They analyze halo DM contributions, vary feedback strength, halo mass, and f_CGM, and examine the solar position's impact on DM uncertainty.
AI.result: Median all-sky halo DMs range from 19-39 pc cm⁻³. With enhanced circumgalactic resolution, mean halo DMs are lower with more sky anisotropy than previous models, reaching <10 pc cm⁻³ toward the poles. DM estimates vary even at fixed feedback, halo mass, and f_CGM.
AI.conclusion: The simulation-based MW halo DM estimates provide a critical baseline for interpreting future FRB observations and understanding the global gas distribution in the Universe. The authors provide a Python package accessible via API functions of Galactic longitude and latitude.

title: Outflows in the Early Universe: Neutral gas Absorption in Galaxies at z > 3 from low-resolution JWST Spectroscopy
summary: Recent JWST/NIRSpec observations have shown that Na I D absorption tracing neutral gas outflows is widespread in massive galaxies at Cosmic Noon ($z\sim2$-$3$), but their prevalence at higher redshift remains largely unexplored. Here we investigate whether similar outflows are already in place during the first 2 Gyr of cosmic history ($z>3$), using a sample of 811 galaxies at $3<z<7$ from the public DAWN JWST Archive and the Mirage or Miracle survey, with secure spectroscopic redshifts and continuum SNR$>5$ in their JWST/NIRSpec PRISM low-resolution spectra ($R\sim100$). We derived physical properties and star formation histories via Prospector SED fitting and isolated the Na I D feature in each spectrum by subtracting the best-fit stellar continuum. We detect an excess of Na I D absorption in 20 galaxies, almost all at $3<z<5$ with stellar mass $>10^{10} M_\odot$, an overall detection fraction of $\sim2.5\%$. The detection fraction rises steeply with stellar mass and quiescence, reaching $\sim11\%$ among the most massive galaxies and $\sim43\%$ among massive quenched systems. The Na I D equivalent widths are large, spanning 4 to 16 Angstrom, and are highest in dusty star-forming galaxies. In previous medium-resolution observations, EWs above 5 Angstrom were mostly found in outflowing gas; we thus interpret our detections as mostly tracing neutral outflows, despite the lack of kinematic information at PRISM resolution. A stacking analysis confirms these trends and provides average Na I D EWs for different subsamples. Under conservative assumptions, we estimate mass outflow rates of 4 to 12 $M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$, exceeding the current star formation rate for about 30% of the detected galaxies. We conclude that neutral outflows are likely already present and important in massive galaxies during the first 2 Gyr of cosmic history.

AI.tldr: Using JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectra of 811 galaxies at z>3, this study detects neutral gas outflows (via Na I D absorption) in ~2.5% of sources, primarily in massive (>10^10 M☉) galaxies at 3<z<5. Detection rates rise with mass and quiescence (up to ~43% in massive quenched galaxies). Derived mass outflow rates (4-12 M☉/yr) can exceed star formation rates, indicating neutral outflows were already present and significant in massive galaxies during the first 2 Gyr of cosmic history.
AI.motivation: While neutral gas outflows traced by Na I D are known to be widespread in massive galaxies at z~2-3 (Cosmic Noon), their prevalence at higher redshifts (z>3) remains largely unexplored. This study aims to determine whether such outflows were already in place during the first 2 Gyr of cosmic history.
AI.method: The study uses a sample of 811 galaxies at 3<z<7 from DAWN JWST Archive and Mirage or Miracle survey with secure spectroscopic redshifts and continuum SNR>5 in JWST/NIRSpec PRISM low-resolution spectra (R~100). Physical properties and star formation histories were derived via Prospector SED fitting. The Na I D feature was isolated by subtracting the best-fit stellar continuum. Stacking analysis was also performed to confirm trends.
AI.result: Na I D absorption excess detected in 20 galaxies (overall ~2.5%), almost all at 3<z<5 with stellar mass >10^10 M☉. Detection fraction rises steeply with mass and quiescence (~11% among most massive, ~43% among massive quenched). Equivalent widths span 4-16 Å, highest in dusty star-forming galaxies. Mass outflow rates estimated at 4-12 M☉/yr, exceeding current SFR for ~30% of detections.
AI.conclusion: Neutral outflows are likely already present and important in massive galaxies during the first 2 Gyr of cosmic history (z>3), suggesting that feedback mechanisms driving such outflows were operational even at these early epochs.

title: Two stellar clocks, one history: a Gaia colour-magnitude-diagram reconstruction of the solar-neighbourhood star-formation history tested against white dwarfs
comment: 12 pages, 9 figures. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: The solar-neighbourhood star-formation history (SFH) can be constrained from the colour-magnitude diagram (CMD) of non-degenerate stars and tested independently with the white-dwarf luminosity function (WDLF). These two tracers sample complementary evolutionary phases and provide a consistency check on both the recovered SFH and the adopted WD cooling models. We reconstruct the local SFH from the Gaia DR3 CMD and test whether the resulting history reproduces the observed 40 pc WDLF. We fit non-degenerate stars in a cylinder of radius 200 pc and vertical extent $\pm40$ pc using the SFERA synthetic-population code. The fit is performed with the PISA and PARSEC stellar libraries. Each CMD-derived solution is then used to generate a synthetic WD population for comparison with the 40 pc WDLF, adopting the same initial-final mass relation and four WD cooling model sets: BaSTI, MIST, La Plata, and Montreal. The two CMD-based solutions agree on the main features of the local SFH: low activity at the oldest ages, an early episode around 9-11 Gyr ago, reduced activity between about 4 and 9 Gyr, and enhanced star formation over the last few Gyr. The predicted WDLFs reproduce the bright and intermediate part of the observed distribution for all cooling grids, but differ substantially around the WDLF maximum and along the faint tail. MIST and BaSTI shift too much weight to magnitudes fainter than the observed maximum, whereas La Plata gives the closest match to the faint tail but leaves larger residuals around the maximum. Montreal provides the best overall compromise. On this cooling scale, progressively removing the oldest synthetic WDs shows that the faint tail disfavours a substantial contribution from WDs with total ages older than about 11 Gyr.

AI.tldr: The paper reconstructs the local star-formation history from Gaia DR3 colour-magnitude diagrams and tests it against the 40 pc white-dwarf luminosity function using multiple WD cooling models. The SFH shows low old-age activity, an early burst 9-11 Gyr ago, a dip 4-9 Gyr ago, and recent enhancement. WDLF predictions vary by cooling model; Montreal performs best overall, and the faint tail suggests minimal WD contribution from ages >11 Gyr.
AI.motivation: To independently constrain the solar-neighbourhood star-formation history using two complementary tracers (CMD and WDLF) and to test the consistency of both the recovered SFH and white-dwarf cooling models.
AI.method: Fit non-degenerate stars in a cylinder (radius 200 pc, height ±40 pc) from Gaia DR3 using the SFERA code with PISA and PARSEC libraries. Generate synthetic WD populations from the CMD-derived SFH using four cooling model grids (BaSTI, MIST, La Plata, Montreal) and compare with the observed 40 pc WDLF.
AI.result: Both CMD solutions agree on SFH features. Predicted WDLFs match bright/intermediate parts but diverge at the maximum and faint tail. MIST/BaSTI overpredict faint WDs; La Plata matches the faint tail best but has larger residuals at the maximum; Montreal gives the best overall fit. The faint tail disfavors significant WD contribution from ages >11 Gyr.
AI.conclusion: Combined CMD and WDLF analysis provides a powerful consistency check on SFH and WD cooling models. The WDLF faint tail sets an upper limit on the oldest WD population, and Montreal cooling models best reconcile the two independent tracers.

title: A Naked Dwarf: Molecular Gas in the Completely Stripped HI Tail of VCC 1249
comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables, accepted for publication in ApJL
summary: We present the first observational hints of the severe removal of both molecular and HI gas from the dwarf galaxy VCC 1249. This extreme stripping event is thought to be driven by the combined effects of tidal interaction and ram pressure. Using deep CO (2$-$1) observations from the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope (JCMT), we obtained marginal CO detections in three regions within the stripped HI tail, with molecular masses of $\sim$10$^{5}$ to 10$^{6}$$M_{\odot}$, comparable to typical masses of giant molecular clouds. In contrast, we did not find CO emission within the stellar disk of VCC 1249. This indicates the severe removal of cold gas, which likely caused the sudden cessation of star formation in the galaxy. This identifies VCC 1249 as a unique laboratory for witnessing the rapid, environmentally-driven quenching of a dwarf galaxy. Our findings provide a critical observational link between gas removal mechanisms and the dramatic phase transition of cluster dwarfs from star-forming to quiescent systems.

AI.tldr: VCC 1249 is a dwarf galaxy experiencing extreme removal of both molecular and HI gas due to combined tidal and ram pressure effects. CO detections in the stripped HI tail (but not in the stellar disk) reveal molecular gas masses of ~10⁵-10⁶ M☉, indicating severe cold gas loss that caused rapid star formation cessation, providing observational evidence linking gas removal to environmental quenching of cluster dwarfs.
AI.motivation: To provide observational evidence for the rapid, environmentally-driven quenching of dwarf galaxies by demonstrating the severe removal of both molecular and atomic gas through combined tidal and ram pressure stripping.
AI.method: Deep CO (2-1) observations using the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope (JCMT) to detect molecular gas in the stripped HI tail and stellar disk of VCC 1249.
AI.result: Marginal CO detections in three regions within the stripped HI tail with molecular masses of ~10⁵ to 10⁶ M☉ (comparable to giant molecular clouds), but no CO emission detected within the stellar disk.
AI.conclusion: VCC 1249 serves as a unique laboratory for witnessing rapid environmental quenching; the findings establish a critical observational link between gas removal mechanisms and the phase transition of cluster dwarfs from star-forming to quiescent systems.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian inference with compositional score modeling for stellar streams
summary: Context: Stellar streams trace the gravitational potential of the Milky Way over a wide range of Galactocentric radii. Since different streams sample different regions of the Galaxy, combining several of them can constrain the global mass distribution more tightly than modeling any single stream in isolation. Most of the existing multi-stream analyses rely on likelihood-based methods that require a new inference run whenever additional streams or kinematic measurements become available. Aims: We aim to infer the Milky Way potential from multiple stellar streams combined with an additional constraint through the Galactic circular velocity curve within a single hierarchical framework. Methods: We model the problem hierarchically, separating parameters that are common to all streams from parameters that are specific to each progenitor. We train score-based neural posterior estimators on a library of simulated streams and combine information from different streams through compositional score modeling as a post-training step. Results: Tests on independent simulations show that the inferred posteriors are well calibrated and accurate. Combining several streams reduces the uncertainties on the global potential parameters relative to single-stream analyses. Applied to Gaia data, the model favours a mildly oblate dark matter halo with axis ratio $q_{NFW} = 0.77$, scale radius $a_{NFW} = 9.3$ kpc, a disk mass of $4.3 \times 10^{10} M_\odot$, and a local dark matter density $ρ_{NFW,\odot} = 0.01153 M_\odot pc^{-3}$ consistent with recent stream-based studies. Conclusions: This hierarchical framework provides a practical way to combine information from multiple stellar streams without repeating the full inference procedure for each new dataset. The method is adaptable to new datasets, like future Gaia DR4, or new spectroscopic surveys, with minimal computational cost.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a hierarchical framework using score-based neural posterior estimators to combine multiple stellar streams for inferring the Milky Way gravitational potential. The method avoids re-running inference when new streams or data become available, and when applied to Gaia data it yields a mildly oblate dark matter halo with specific parameter values.
AI.motivation: Existing multi-stream analyses rely on likelihood-based methods that require a new inference run whenever additional streams or kinematic measurements become available. The authors aim to infer the Milky Way potential from multiple stellar streams combined with the Galactic circular velocity curve within a single hierarchical framework that can be updated without repeating the full inference.
AI.method: The problem is modeled hierarchically, separating global (common) parameters from progenitor-specific parameters. Score-based neural posterior estimators are trained on a library of simulated streams, and information from different streams is combined through compositional score modeling as a post-training step.
AI.result: Tests on independent simulations show well-calibrated and accurate posteriors. Combining multiple streams reduces uncertainties on global potential parameters compared to single-stream analyses. Applied to Gaia data, the model yields: oblate dark matter halo with axis ratio q_NFW = 0.77, scale radius a_NFW = 9.3 kpc, disk mass 4.3×10^10 M_sun, and local dark matter density ρ_NFW,⊙ = 0.01153 M_sun pc^{-3}.
AI.conclusion: This hierarchical framework provides a practical way to combine information from multiple stellar streams without repeating the full inference for each new dataset. The method is adaptable to new datasets (e.g., Gaia DR4) or new spectroscopic surveys with minimal computational cost.

title: Observations of High Galactic Latitude Line and Continuum Emission (912 - 1600 Å) with New Horizons
summary: We present observations of the cosmic ultraviolet background (CUVB) from 912 - 1600 A using the Stem aperture of the Alice spectrograph on the New Horizons spacecraft at 56 AU from the Sun, providing a spectral resolution of 9 A for diffuse sources. We detect emission lines of CIII (977 A) and CIV (1548/1551 A) at the 3 sigma level with strengths of 4200 +/- 1500 and 4100 +/- 1200 ph cm(-2) s(-1) sr(-1), respectively, and a marginal detection of OVI (1032/1038 A) at 1400 +/- 1300 ph cm(-2) s(-1) sr(-1). We report a 3 sigma detection of an emission line at 1135 A, which we have identified with the N I resonance triplet. Although this line had earlier been observed in FUSE and SPEAR data, it had been attributed to airglow or instrumental effects. We confirm, for the first time, that it must originate in the Galaxy. The dust-scattered continuum is dominated by a small number (N < 100) of O9 - B2 stars and shows the deep absorption feature near 1000 A seen in the stellar spectrum. Our models suggest an albedo of a < 0.5 over most of the spectrum (950 -- 1550 A) for the dust grains with the phase function asymmetry of g < 0.6. We find an offset, comprising the extragalactic background light and halo contributors, consistent with our earlier results from the Box, including the decline in the offset near the Lyman limit. We confirm that much of the emission must be from an unidentified component of the CUVB.

AI.tldr: New Horizons/Alice spectrograph observations at 56 AU reveal the cosmic UV background (912-1600 Å) with detections of CIII, CIV, OVI lines, and a first-ever confirmed Galactic N I triplet at 1135 Å. Dust-scattered continuum from <100 O9-B2 stars shows low albedo (<0.5) and asymmetry (<0.6). An offset consistent with extragalactic background plus halo contributors is found, confirming an unidentified CUVB component.
AI.motivation: To measure the cosmic ultraviolet background (CUVB) free from airglow and solar system contamination by exploiting New Horizons' distant vantage point at 56 AU.
AI.method: Utilized the Alice spectrograph's Stem aperture on New Horizons at 56 AU to acquire diffuse UV spectra from 912–1600 Å at 9 Å resolution, with emission line fitting and dust-scattering modeling.
AI.result: Detected CIII (977 Å) and CIV (1548/1551 Å) at ~3σ, marginal OVI; confirmed Galactic N I triplet at 1135 Å (3σ). Dust albedo <0.5, phase asymmetry g<0.6. Offset includes extragalactic background light (EBL) and halo, declining near Lyman limit.
AI.conclusion: A significant portion of the CUVB remains unidentified beyond known stellar, dust-scattered, and extragalactic components.

title: Accurate Extragalactic Magnetic Fields from Faraday Rotation with Optimal Dispersion Measure Estimators
summary: Faraday rotation measures (RMs) are one of our few observational tools for measuring magnetic field strengths in extragalactic systems, but converting an RM to a magnetic field estimate requires knowledge of the electron column density -- the dispersion measure (DM) -- to the RM source. Because DMs are difficult to measure for most extragalactic radio galaxies, observers have adopted a range of strategies to estimate them from more easily measured quantities, but the accuracy of these approaches is poorly known. To address this, we carry out simulated observations of high-resolution magnetohydrodynamic simulations of a range of galactic environments to explore the performance of various possible DM estimators. We obtain the best results using an estimator $\mathrm{DM} \propto \mathrm{EM}^α \ N_\mathrm{Hi}^β$, where EM is the emission measure and $N_\mathrm{Hi}$ is the atomic hydrogen column density, with exponents $α\approx 0.2-0.4$ and $β\approx 0-0.1$ depending on galactic environment (e.g., galaxy centres versus outskirts, and dwarfs versus spirals). We show that the variation of these exponents with environment can be understood in terms of simple physical arguments. Based on our tests, we provide recommended best practices for extracting galactic magnetic fields from RM data as a function of galactic environment and of proxy data availability, and show that using these methods one can obtain field measurements that are accurate to a few tenths of a dex. This work therefore represents an important step toward making use of RM data from next-generation surveys with the SKA.

AI.tldr: The paper uses MHD simulations to test estimators for converting Faraday rotation measures (RMs) into magnetic field estimates, finding an optimal DM estimator based on EM and HI column density, and provides best practices for accurate magnetic field measurements in different galactic environments.
AI.motivation: Converting Faraday rotation measures to magnetic field estimates requires knowledge of electron column density (DM), which is difficult to measure for extragalactic radio galaxies; the accuracy of existing proxy-based estimators is poorly known, motivating a systematic evaluation.
AI.method: Simulated observations of high-resolution MHD simulations of various galactic environments were performed to test different DM estimators. The optimal estimator scales as DM ∝ EM^α N_HI^β, with environment-dependent exponents (α ≈ 0.2-0.4, β ≈ 0-0.1).
AI.result: The best-performing estimator uses emission measure (EM) and atomic hydrogen column density (N_HI) with exponents α ≈ 0.2-0.4 and β ≈ 0-0.1, varying with galactic environment. The variation is explainable by simple physical arguments. Magnetic field measurements accurate to a few tenths of a dex are achievable.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides recommended best practices for extracting galactic magnetic fields from RM data depending on galactic environment and data availability, representing an important step toward utilizing RM data from next-generation SKA surveys.

title: Isotropic deceleration and near-zero baseline acceleration in Pantheon+ supernovae: new arguments in the dark energy debate
summary: We perform four independent decompositions of the deceleration parameter $q_0$ using 1564 Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) from the Pantheon+ catalogue: by redshift bin, sky hemisphere, host galaxy mass, and supernova colour. Without any progenitor age correction, the full sample yields $q_m$ = - 0.062 -- far below the $Λ$CDM expectation of - 0.55 -- challenging the standard picture before any correction. Crucially, the sky hemisphere test shows the deceleration is equally strong in the CMB dipole ($q_m$ = + 1.45) and anti-dipole hemispheres (+ 1.55), directly contradicting the SRS26 anisotropy argument. Our results challenge both current interpretations.

AI.tldr: Using 1564 SNe Ia from Pantheon+, four independent decompositions of $q_0$ (by redshift, sky hemisphere, host mass, SN colour) show $q_m=-0.062$ without progenitor age correction, far below $Λ$CDM's -0.55. Sky hemisphere test shows equal deceleration in CMB dipole (+1.45) and anti-dipole (+1.55) hemispheres, contradicting SRS26 anisotropy claims.
AI.motivation: To challenge standard $Λ$CDM predictions of the deceleration parameter $q_0$ by performing multiple independent decompositions using Pantheon+ SNe Ia data, testing both the overall value and directional anisotropy claims.
AI.method: Four independent decompositions of $q_0$ from 1564 Pantheon+ SNe Ia: redshift binning, sky hemisphere (CMB dipole vs anti-dipole), host galaxy mass, and supernova colour. No progenitor age correction applied.
AI.result: Full sample yields $q_m=-0.062$, well below $Λ$CDM expectation of -0.55. Sky hemispheres show nearly equal deceleration (+1.45 dipole, +1.55 anti-dipole), contradicting SRS26 anisotropy arguments.
AI.conclusion: Results challenge both the standard $Λ$CDM picture and the SRS26 anisotropy interpretation.

title: Dissecting the multiple-component outflow in NGC 5548 with absorption-line Variability
summary: AGN-driven outflows are routinely invoked as a key agent of supermassive black holes to regulate the evolution of galaxies. The radial distance from the central engine is a crucial parameter for evaluating the impact of these outflows on the host galaxy. In this work, we estimate the radial distances of ultraviolet (UV) outflow components in NGC 5548 using the most up-to-date absorption-line variability method, combined with multi-epoch HST/COS spectroscopy from the 2014 AGN STORM campaign and archival data observed in 2013. The recombination timescale (tr) of the absorbers are measured by analyzing the detection rate curves of absorption-line variability. In particular, the detection rate curves of the absorption troughs showing blended multiple velocity components are featured by distinct ``multi-step' profiles, allowing for measuring tr for individual components. Among the 6 identified outflow components, four are found to be a few pc from the center and two are 30-40 pc away. Our results agree well with the more reliable results in the literature on components 1 and 4, and show overall consistency with previous works, demonstrating the power of our new methodology especially when it is aided by densely sampled HST spectra.

AI.tldr: Using UV absorption-line variability methods with HST/COS data, researchers estimated radial distances of 6 outflow components in NGC 5548: four at a few parsecs and two at 30-40 parsecs from the central engine, demonstrating a new "multi-step" detection rate methodology for blended velocity components.
AI.motivation: To determine the radial distances of UV outflow components in NGC 5548, which is crucial for evaluating the impact of AGN-driven outflows on host galaxy evolution.
AI.method: Applied an absorption-line variability method using recombination timescale (tr) measurements from detection rate curves, featuring a novel "multi-step" profile analysis for blended multiple velocity components, using multi-epoch HST/COS spectroscopy from the 2014 AGN STORM campaign and 2013 archival data.
AI.result: Six outflow components identified: four at a few pc and two at 30-40 pc from the center. Results agree with literature for components 1 and 4, showing overall consistency with previous works.
AI.conclusion: The new methodology, particularly with densely sampled HST spectra, effectively measures radial distances of outflow components, demonstrating power for blended velocity components.

title: Gravitational Lensing Predictions from Wave Simulations of Fuzzy Dark Matter
summary: In the cold dark matter paradigm, ultra-light particles are emerging as strong contenders to conventional massive particles. A unique prediction of dark matter comprising such ultra-light particles, known as fuzzy dark matter (FDM), is the presence of strong density modulations throughout galactic halos due to wave interference, which -- when approximated by a Gaussian random field (GRF) -- have been proposed to account for the inability to reproduce the observed positions (when measured at sufficient precisions) and flux ratios of multiply-lensed images of quasars. Here, we predict for the first time the properties of gravitationally lensed images generated from 3-D density fields obtained by wave simulations that directly evolve the Schrödinger--Poisson equations. Using a novel framework to project these evolved density fields along various axes of the 3-D halo, we obtain the distribution of perturbations to the positions of lensed images. As an exacting test, we find that particles of mass $10^{-22}$ eV can reproduce the positions of the quadruply-lensed radio jets in system HS 0810+2554 to a level better than that of either the GRF approximation or, to a greater extent, an NFW best-fit solution, both of which rely on accurately capturing the global 3-D density field of dark matter halos. Our work highlights the importance of wave simulations for making accurate FDM lensing predictions and the potential for high-resolution observations of lensed systems to serve as a direct probe of the nature of dark matter.

AI.tldr: This paper uses 3-D wave simulations of fuzzy dark matter (FDM) to predict gravitational lensing effects, finding that particles of mass $10^{-22}$ eV reproduce observed quadruply-lensed radio jet positions in HS 0810+2554 better than Gaussian random field approximations or NFW profiles, highlighting wave simulations' importance for accurate FDM lensing predictions.
AI.motivation: To determine whether fuzzy dark matter (ultra-light particles) can explain observed positions and flux ratios of multiply-lensed quasar images, which conventional cold dark matter models struggle to reproduce at sufficient precision.
AI.method: The authors evolve 3-D density fields using Schrödinger-Poisson wave simulations, project them along various axes of the 3-D halo using a novel framework, and compute perturbations to lensed image positions. They compare results against the Gaussian random field approximation and NFW best-fit solutions using the HS 0810+2554 lensed system.
AI.result: FDM particles of mass $10^{-22}$ eV reproduce the positions of quadruply-lensed radio jets in HS 0810+2554 better than both the GRF approximation and the NFW best-fit solution.
AI.conclusion: Wave simulations are essential for making accurate FDM lensing predictions, and high-resolution observations of lensed systems can serve as a direct probe of the nature of dark matter.

title: A RELHIC twin candidate near the galaxy M51
comment: 8 figures, 1 table, 8 pages; accepted for publication in Astronomy and Astrophysics
summary:
We report the discovery of a pair of H I clouds near M51 (NGC 5194) using the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST). These clouds have no optical counterparts and are potential candidates for Reionization-Limited H I Clouds (RELHICs).
  We search for compact H I sources in deep FEASTS observations using SoFiA and remove objects with optical counterparts through cross-matching with the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. The remaining candidates are modelled as hydrostatic H I structures embedded in Navarro-Frenk-White dark matter haloes and compared with RELHIC predictions and TNG50 simulations.
  We identify two H I clouds, Cloud S and Cloud N, at projected distances of 70--90 kpc from M51. Each cloud has an H I mass of approximately 10^6.5 solar masses, a velocity dispersion of about 20 km/s, and no detectable optical counterpart down to a g-band surface brightness limit of approximately 27.5 mag arcsec^-2. Their stellar luminosities are constrained to be below 10^5 solar luminosities. Their H I properties are consistent with RELHIC predictions, corresponding to host halo masses of 3.7 +- 0.4 * 10^9 solar masses.
  Cloud S and Cloud N are promising but not definitive RELHIC candidates. A tidal origin remains possible in the interacting M51 system, especially because the clouds are unresolved by FAST and Cloud N may show a velocity gradient. Future high-resolution interferometric observations will be crucial for distinguishing between starless dark matter haloes and tidal debris.

AI.tldr: Using FAST, we discovered two H I clouds near M51 with no optical counterparts, consistent with RELHIC predictions (halo masses ~3.7×10^9 M☉), but a tidal origin cannot be ruled out; higher-resolution follow-up is needed.
AI.motivation: To search for Reionization-Limited H I Clouds (RELHICs) — starless, dark-matter-dominated H I structures that survived reionization — as a probe of small-scale dark matter haloes and galaxy formation physics.
AI.method: Compact H I sources were identified from FEASTS/FAST data using SoFiA, then cross-matched with DESI Legacy Surveys to remove optical counterparts. Candidates were modeled as hydrostatic H I embedded in NFW dark matter haloes and compared to RELHIC predictions and TNG50 simulations.
AI.result: Two H I clouds (Cloud S and Cloud N) were detected at 70–90 kpc from M51, each with ~10^6.5 M☉ H I mass, ~20 km/s velocity dispersion, no optical counterpart down to g~27.5 mag arcsec⁻², and stellar luminosity <10^5 L☉. Their properties match RELHIC models with host halo masses of 3.7±0.4×10^9 M☉.
AI.conclusion: Cloud S and N are promising but not definitive RELHICs; a tidal origin in the interacting M51 system remains possible. High-resolution interferometric follow-up is required to distinguish between starless dark matter haloes and tidal debris.

title: What could an emerging Big Bang Nucleosynthesis discrepancy be hinting at?
summary: The latest measurement of the primordial deuterium abundance is in $\sim 2σ$ tension with several state-of-the-art predictions of standard Big Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN), when using the baryon density inferred from the $Λ$CDM model fit to cosmic microwave background (CMB) data. This tension increases to $\sim 3σ$ for models attempting to solve the Hubble tension, such as early dark energy (EDE), which generally predict a larger baryon density than in $Λ$CDM. We test whether this discrepancy could be pointing to a non-standard expansion history during BBN. We compute light-element abundances with PRIMAT and compare $Λ$CDM, a $ΔN_{\rm eff}$ extension, and a very early dark energy (vEDE) component. For vEDE, we sample $ΔH/H$, the fractional increase of the expansion rate while deuterium burning is freezing out and helium-4 fusion is mostly over. The Bayesian analysis using BBN plus the CMB baryon-density constraint in the EDE cosmology gives $ΔH/H = 0.087^{+0.036}_{-0.037}$ during the deuterium burning epoch, i.e. at a temperature $T_{\rm D}\simeq0.03\,{\rm MeV}$, and no residual tension. The vEDE component preserves the observed deuterium abundance at the larger CMB baryon density while only mildly affecting helium-4. By contrast, extra radiation raises the helium-4 abundance too efficiently and does not reconcile the baryon density determinations. Together with inflation, dark energy, and EDE, our results hint at the presence of another light scalar field in cosmology.

AI.tldr: The ~2σ tension between primordial deuterium measurements and standard BBN predictions (using ΛCDM baryon density from CMB) increases to ~3σ in Hubble-tension solutions like EDE. A Bayesian analysis with BBN + CMB constraints in EDE cosmology finds that a very early dark energy (vEDE) component with ΔH/H = 0.087⁺⁰·⁰³⁶₋₀·⁰³⁷ during deuterium burning resolves the tension without overproducing helium-4, unlike extra radiation (ΔN_eff). This hints at an additional light scalar field in cosmology.
AI.motivation: The primordial deuterium abundance measurement shows a ~2σ tension with standard BBN predictions when using the ΛCDM CMB-inferred baryon density, and this tension worsens to ~3σ in EDE models that aim to resolve the Hubble tension. The paper investigates whether this discrepancy signals a non-standard expansion history during BBN.
AI.method: Light-element abundances are computed using PRIMAT. The study compares ΛCDM, a ΔN_eff extension, and a very early dark energy (vEDE) component. For vEDE, the fractional increase ΔH/H of the expansion rate during deuterium burning freeze-out is sampled. A Bayesian analysis is performed using BBN data plus the CMB baryon-density constraint within the EDE cosmology.
AI.result: The Bayesian analysis gives ΔH/H = 0.087⁺⁰·⁰³⁶₋₀·⁰³⁷ during the deuterium burning epoch (T_D ≈ 0.03 MeV), with no residual tension. vEDE preserves the observed deuterium abundance at the higher CMB baryon density while only mildly affecting helium-4. In contrast, extra radiation (ΔN_eff) raises helium-4 too efficiently and cannot reconcile the baryon density determinations.
AI.conclusion: A vEDE component that modifies the expansion rate during BBN can resolve the deuterium abundance tension without overproducing helium-4. Along with inflation, dark energy, and EDE, this hints at the presence of another light scalar field in cosmology.

title: Measuring Outflow Distances in NGC 5548 Using Absorption-Line Variability Diagnostics
summary: AGN-driven outflows serve as a key channel through which the energetic central engine influences host galaxy evolution. Among the physical properties of outflows, their radial distance from the galactic nucleus is particularly important for assessing AGN feedback. In this study, we investigate the UV outflow components in NGC 5548 by analyzing the variability of C IV absorption troughs in optical spectra obtained through multiple HST observations during 2013 and 2014. We construct a set of variability-based diagnostic events, labeled G1 and G2, which are sensitive to the recombination timescale ($t_r$) of ionized gas. By combining these with mock light curves generated using a damped random walk (DRW) model, we numerically establish a mapping between the G1 event probability and $t_r$. This approach allows us to constrain the radial distances of outflow components 1 and 6, whose absorption variability is primarily driven by changes in the incident ionizing continuum, to be $0.77^{+0.10}_{-0.10}$ and $1.72^{+1.74}_{-1.72}$ pc, respectively. These results are consistent with those obtained using a different method in our previous study, as well as with values reported in the literature.

AI.tldr: Using HST UV spectra of NGC 5548, this study develops variability-based diagnostics (G1/G2 events) combined with DRW simulations to constrain the radial distances of two C IV outflow components to ~0.77 pc and ~1.72 pc, consistent with prior methods.
AI.motivation: The radial distance of AGN-driven outflows from the galactic nucleus is a critical but uncertain parameter for assessing AGN feedback on host galaxy evolution.
AI.method: Construct variability-based diagnostic events (G1, G2) sensitive to recombination timescale t_r from HST/C IV absorption trough variability in NGC 5548; combine with DRW mock light curves to numerically map G1 event probability to t_r and thereby constrain outflow distances.
AI.result: Outflow component 1 distance = 0.77^{+0.10}_{-0.10} pc; component 6 distance = 1.72^{+1.74}_{-1.72} pc.
AI.conclusion: The derived distances are consistent with prior methods and literature, validating the variability-based diagnostic approach for constraining AGN outflow locations.

title: The correlation between voids identified in 3D large-scale-structure and 2D weak-lensing maps
summary: We investigate the correspondence between voids identified in the 3D halo distribution and those detected in WL convergence maps. We used 108 realizations of the full-sky lensing simulations, populated with a source galaxy redshift distribution consistent with the Dark Energy Survey Year 3 sample. Catalogs of 3D halo voids and WL voids were constructed using the VIDE and tunnel algorithms, respectively. The spatial association between the two populations was quantified by measuring the angular excess number density of halo voids around WL void centers. We detected a statistically significant (S/N >= 25) positive correlation between WL voids and low-redshift halo voids (0 < z_hv < 0.5) at small angular separations, indicating that WL voids trace genuine underdensities in the large-scale matter distribution. The correlation amplitude closely depends on the WL void selection scheme and decreases when stringent peak-amplitude thresholds are applied, thereby reducing the number of detected WL voids and broadening their effective sizes. The signal also displays a strong redshift dependence: halo voids at higher redshift exhibit weaker correlations because of the declining efficiency of the WL kernel, while WL voids identified from higher-redshift source bins produce stronger correlations due to the increased contribution from line-of-sight structures. We additionally examined the impact of halo-void morphology and found that rounder voids with a weaker alignment along the line of sight display marginally stronger associations with WL voids. Our results provide new insights into the contribution of 3D structure to WL-selected underdensities and offer guidance for future observational analyses seeking to interpret WL voids as tracers of the matter field.

AI.tldr: The study examines the correspondence between 3D halo voids and weak lensing (WL) voids using full-sky lensing simulations with DES Year 3 source galaxy distribution. Results show significant (S/N ≥ 25) positive correlation between WL voids and low-redshift halo voids (z < 0.5), with correlation strength depending on WL void selection scheme, redshift, and halo-void morphology. WL voids trace genuine matter underdensities, but the signal weakens with stringent peak-amplitude thresholds, higher halo-void redshift, and stronger line-of-sight alignment.
AI.motivation: To understand whether weak lensing voids, which are projected 2D underdensities, correspond to genuine 3D matter underdensities traced by halos, and to quantify the factors affecting this correspondence for future observational studies.
AI.method: Used 108 full-sky lensing simulation realizations with DES Y3 source redshift distribution. 3D halo voids identified via VIDE algorithm; WL voids identified via tunnel algorithm. Spatial association quantified by angular excess number density of halo voids around WL void centers.
AI.result: Significant (S/N ≥ 25) positive correlation between WL voids and low-redshift halo voids (0 < z_hv < 0.5). Correlation amplitude depends on WL void selection scheme, decreases with stringent peak-amplitude thresholds. Strong redshift dependence: higher halo-void redshift weakens correlation; higher source-bin redshift strengthens it. Rounder, less line-of-sight-aligned voids show marginally stronger associations.
AI.conclusion: WL voids trace genuine 3D matter underdensities at low redshift. The redshift dependence and morphological dependence offer guidance for interpreting WL voids as matter field tracers in future observational analyses.

title: MIGHTEE: The Host-Galaxy Associated Catalogue of the Radio Sources in MIGHTEE Continuum Data Release 1
comment: 23 pages, 13 figures, Accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: Radio continuum surveys provide samples of active galactic nuclei (AGN) and star forming galaxies (SFGs) to high redshifts, free of biases due to dust obscuration. However, radio detected sources require multi-wavelength counterparts to understand their intrinsic properties (e.g. redshift, stellar mass) and to study the evolution of star formation and AGN activity. In this work we present host galaxy counterparts for the MeerKAT International GHz Tiered Extragalactic Exploration (MIGHTEE) survey continuum Data Release 1 in regions with the best ancillary data (totalling 7.5 sq. deg). We combine statistical cross-matching and visual inspection to identify Ks-band selected host galaxies, and additionally combine multiple radio components into single physical objects, where needed. This results in a combined radio catalogue of ~66 000 sources, with host counterparts and redshifts identified for ~95 per cent of sources in the COSMOS field, ~91 per cent in XMM-LSS and ~90 per cent in CDFS-DEEP. This includes a significant fraction of sources with spectroscopic redshifts within the COSMOS field (~50 per cent), with ~30 and ~20 per cent in the XMM-LSS and CDFS-DEEP fields respectively. Using the cross-matched catalogue, we make an initial identification of radio-excess and star forming galaxies based on comparisons of the radio luminosities to host star formation rates. Using this split as a proxy for radio loud AGN or SFGs, we present expectations for the redshift distributions of these sources, finding broad agreement with those from deep radio luminosity functions and simulated catalogues.

AI.tldr: This paper presents host galaxy counterparts for ~66,000 radio sources from the MIGHTEE survey Data Release 1 across 7.5 sq. deg, achieving >90% identification rates via statistical cross-matching and visual inspection. It provides redshift distributions and an initial classification of radio-excess AGN vs. star-forming galaxies, finding broad agreement with deep radio luminosity functions.
AI.motivation: Radio continuum surveys provide unbiased samples of AGN and SFGs at high redshifts, but radio-detected sources require multi-wavelength counterparts to derive intrinsic properties (redshift, stellar mass) for studying galaxy and AGN evolution.
AI.method: Combined statistical cross-matching and visual inspection to identify Ks-band selected host galaxies, merged multiple radio components into single physical objects, and used radio luminosity vs. star formation rate comparisons to classify radio-excess AGN versus SFGs.
AI.result: Produced a catalogue of ~66,000 sources with host counterparts identified for ~95% (COSMOS), ~91% (XMM-LSS), and ~90% (CDFS-DEEP), including ~50%, ~30%, and ~20% spectroscopic redshifts respectively. Redshift distributions agree with deep radio luminosity functions and simulations.
AI.conclusion: The cross-matched catalogue enables robust classification of radio-excess AGN and SFGs, with redshift distributions consistent with expected evolutionary trends from luminosity functions and simulations.

title: When galaxies burst II. Implications of enhanced burstiness for the 21-cm Cosmic Dawn signal
summary: Recent JWST observations suggest that star formation in the early universe was substantially burstier than assumed in standard models. Such burstiness can be described as a stochastic process characterized by the burst amplitude and the coherence time of star formation epochs. In this paper, we investigate how bursty star formation modifies the 21-cm power spectrum during Cosmic Dawn through its impact on the non-local radiation fields that govern its evolution, namely Lyman-$α$ and X-ray backgrounds. To do so, we introduce an unequal-time correlation in the star-formation-rate density sourcing the two fields and we compute its impact using the analytical framework implemented in the public code Zeus21. We find that the burstiness-induced time correlation produces a shot-noise-like contribution in the Lyman-$α$ and X-ray fields, enhancing both their auto- and cross-power spectra while leaving the global 21-cm signal, $T_{21}(z)$, unchanged. As a result, the 21-cm power spectrum is strongly modified by a shot-noise-like contribution at the beginning of the Cosmic Dawn, where the signal is dominated by lower-mass halos ($M_h\lesssim10^{10}\,M_\odot$), and is boosted by a factor of a few near the Wouthuysen-Field absorption trough. Elsewhere at low redshift, where the clustering signal dominates and larger halos drive the signal, the burstiness component is negligible.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how bursty star formation in the early universe, characterized by stochastic variations in star-formation-rate density, modifies the 21-cm power spectrum during Cosmic Dawn through its impact on Lyman-α and X-ray backgrounds. Using the Zeus21 analytical framework with an unequal-time correlation model, the authors find that burstiness introduces a shot-noise-like contribution that enhances the 21-cm power spectrum at high redshifts (lower-mass halos) and near the Wouthuysen-Field absorption trough, while being negligible at lower redshifts where clustering dominates.
AI.motivation: Recent JWST observations suggest star formation in the early universe was substantially burstier than standard models assume, motivating a need to understand how such burstiness affects observable signatures like the 21-cm signal.
AI.method: The authors introduce an unequal-time correlation in the star-formation-rate density sourcing Lyman-α and X-ray fields, and compute its impact using the analytical framework implemented in the public code Zeus21.
AI.result: Burstiness-induced time correlation produces a shot-noise-like contribution in Lyman-α and X-ray fields, enhancing their auto- and cross-power spectra while leaving the global 21-cm signal unchanged. The 21-cm power spectrum is strongly modified at the beginning of Cosmic Dawn (boosted near the Wouthuysen-Field absorption trough), but negligible at low redshift where clustering dominates.
AI.conclusion: Bursty star formation significantly impacts the 21-cm power spectrum at high redshifts and near the absorption trough, but not at lower redshifts where larger halos and clustering drive the signal.

title: What's Missing in AGN Feedback? Lessons learnt from Magneticum, IllustrisTNG and Simba
comment: 14 pages, 11 figures + appendix. Modified abstract to match the arXiv guidelines. Accepted by A&A
summary: Accurately balancing gas reservoirs, star formation, and feedback across cosmic time remains a central challenge for galaxy formation models in modern hydrodynamical simulations. While different feedback prescriptions reproduce selected local galaxy properties with varying success, the most pronounced discrepancies emerge in predictions for the hot gas content of dark matter halos. We examine three state-of-the-art cosmological simulations: Magneticum, IllustrisTNG, and SIMBA, which struggle to simultaneously reproduce observed galaxy and halo gas properties in the local Universe. We confront their predictions with spatially resolved galaxy data from MaNGA and recent constraints on the hot gas mass fraction-halo mass (fgas-Mh) relation from eROSITA and Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (SZ) measurements. Reproducing the observed fgas-Mh relation requires strong active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback. However, such feedback often leads to excessive quenching in simulated galaxy populations. Magneticum and SIMBA match the observed gas fraction relation but predict an overabundance of quenched galaxies. In contrast, IllustrisTNG implements weaker AGN feedback, yielding more realistic star-forming fractions but systematically overpredicting hot gas masses in massive groups and poor clusters. Overall, these tensions indicate current feedback models remain incomplete, not only in the total energy injected but also in the timing, location, and coupling of this energy to the surrounding gas. Our results therefore highlight the need to revisit subgrid feedback prescriptions and develop more self-consistent models capable of simultaneously regulating galaxy growth and the thermodynamic properties of halo gas. Motivated by this discrepancy, a companion study will explore whether the feedback strengths required to match halo gas constraints inevitably lead to overquenching and distorted galaxy demographics.

AI.tldr: Three cosmological simulations (Magneticum, IllustrisTNG, SIMBA) struggle to simultaneously reproduce observed galaxy and halo gas properties. Strong AGN feedback matches hot gas constraints but overquenches galaxies; weaker feedback yields realistic star formation but overpredicts hot gas masses. Current feedback models need revision in timing, location, and coupling of energy injection.
AI.motivation: Accurately balancing gas reservoirs, star formation, and feedback across cosmic time remains a central challenge for galaxy formation models in modern hydrodynamical simulations.
AI.method: The study compares three cosmological simulations (Magneticum, IllustrisTNG, SIMBA) against spatially resolved galaxy data from MaNGA and hot gas mass fraction-halo mass constraints from eROSITA and SZ measurements.
AI.result: Magneticum and SIMBA match observed fgas-Mh relation but overpredict quenched galaxies. IllustrisTNG yields more realistic star-forming fractions but overpredicts hot gas masses in massive groups/poor clusters. No simulation simultaneously reproduces both galaxy and halo gas properties.
AI.conclusion: Current feedback models remain incomplete in total energy injected, timing, location, and coupling of energy to surrounding gas. Subgrid feedback prescriptions need revision to develop more self-consistent models that simultaneously regulate galaxy growth and halo gas thermodynamics.

title: Probing the baryonic--dark matter connection in galaxy clusters using X-rays with gated recurrent unit neural networks
comment: 21 pages, 21 figures, 4 tables, submitted to A&A, abstract abridged for arXiv submission, comments welcome
summary: Accurate cluster mass measurements are crucial for cosmology, yet conventional hydrostatic equilibrium (HSE) methods can suffer from systematic biases, particularly in dynamically disturbed systems. We present a gated recurrent unit (GRU) based deep learning framework for predicting three-dimensional mass profiles of galaxy clusters from spherically averaged intra-cluster medium (ICM) radial profiles. By treating ICM profiles as sequential data, the GRU captures radial dependencies and naturally handles profiles with different radial samplings. We train and validate the model using high-resolution hydrodynamical simulations from The Three Hundred Project, achieving unbiased mass predictions with a typical 1$σ$ scatter of $\sim$5% over most of the cluster region, significantly improving upon HSE estimates. The model provides radius-dependent uncertainty estimates and remains robust against variations in data quality and cluster morphology. When trained jointly on independent simulation suites (GIZMO-SIMBA and GADGET-X), it successfully generalises across both simulations. Feature importance analysis shows that enclosed gas mass is the dominant predictor, with pressure and temperature providing additional information on the radial mass distribution. We further apply the GRU model to X-ray observations of the REXCESS and X-COP cluster samples from XMM-Newton and compare the inferred mass profiles with HSE estimates. The HSE masses are systematically lower than the GRU predictions for the higher-mass X-COP sample, while the REXCESS sample shows mass differences that are close to zero on average. This work provides a data-driven framework for cluster mass inference that bridges simulations and observations and can be extended to multi-wavelength datasets, including Sunyaev-Zel'dovich and optical observations.

AI.tldr: A GRU-based deep learning framework predicts 3D mass profiles of galaxy clusters from spherically averaged ICM radial profiles, trained on The Three Hundred Project simulations. It achieves ~5% scatter, outperforms hydrostatic equilibrium estimates, and generalizes across simulations. Applied to XMM-Newton observations, it finds HSE masses are systematically lower for high-mass X-COP clusters but consistent for REXCESS.
AI.motivation: Accurate cluster mass measurements are crucial for cosmology, but conventional hydrostatic equilibrium (HSE) methods suffer from systematic biases, especially in dynamically disturbed clusters.
AI.method: A gated recurrent unit (GRU) based deep learning framework that treats spherically averaged ICM radial profiles (temperature, pressure, enclosed gas mass, etc.) as sequential data to predict 3D mass profiles, with radius-dependent uncertainty estimates.
AI.result: Unbiased mass predictions with ~5% scatter over most of the cluster region, significantly improving upon HSE estimates. The model generalizes across simulation suites. Enclosed gas mass is the dominant predictor. HSE masses are systematically lower for X-COP but consistent for REXCESS.
AI.conclusion: This data-driven framework bridges simulations and observations for cluster mass inference and can be extended to multi-wavelength datasets (SZ, optical).

title: The Stellar Mass Function of Gas-Rich Galaxies and the Underlying $M_{\rm HI}-M_{\rm star}$ Scaling Relation in the Local Universe
summary: We estimate the Galaxy Stellar Mass Function (GSMF) of HI gas-rich galaxies using the 100\% ALFALFA ($α$) catalog, $\sim 98\%$ of which have optical counterparts in the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) and a subset of them have counterparts in GALEX SDSS WISE Legacy Catalogue-2(GSWLC-2). We use the mass estimates from this subset which combines UV, optical and IR bands with individual dust corrections to recalibrate optical stellar mass estimates. We use a non-parametric method to estimate the GSMF of these gas-rich galaxies. The resulting, HI-selected GSMF is consistent with a single Schechter function with best-fit parameters $\left\{φ_* (10^{-3}\, h_{70}^{3}\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-3}\,\mathrm{dex}^{-1}), \log_{10} (M_*/M_{\odot}) + 2\log_{10} h_{70}, α\right\} = \left\{2.30^{+0.12}_{-0.12}, \,10.83^{+0.01}_{-0.01},\, -1.14^{+0.02}_{-0.02}\right\} $. Additionally, the red and blue populations are each well described by a single Schechter function. After correcting for selection effects, we find that the red population accounts for only $\sim18\%$ of gas-rich galaxies by number, yet contributes $\sim54\%$ of the total stellar mass, with the blue population accounting for the rest. Using an optically selected sample and a joint optical-HI sample, we find gas-rich galaxies represent $\sim 33\%$ of the total stellar mass density and $\sim 39\%$ of the total galaxy number counts in the local Universe. We use the GSMF and the HI mass function (HIMF) of the HI-selected sample to obtain the $M_{\rm HI}-M_{\rm star}$ relation, which is free from selection bias.

AI.tldr: This paper estimates the Galaxy Stellar Mass Function (GSMF) for HI gas-rich galaxies using the ALFALFA catalog, recalibrates stellar masses with multi-band data, and finds that gas-rich galaxies account for ~33% of stellar mass density and ~39% of galaxy counts in the local Universe. The HI-selected GSMF follows a Schechter function, and red gas-rich galaxies are rare by number (~18%) but contribute ~54% of stellar mass.
AI.motivation: To characterize the stellar mass distribution of HI gas-rich galaxies, understand their contribution to the local galaxy population, and derive a selection-bias-free HI mass–stellar mass relation.
AI.method: Uses the 100% ALFALFA catalog with SDSS optical counterparts and GALEX/SDSS/WISE photometry (GSWLC-2) for dust-corrected stellar mass estimates; applies a non-parametric GSMF estimator; corrects for selection effects; compares optically selected and joint optical-HI samples to quantify the gas-rich galaxy fraction.
AI.result: HI-selected GSMF fits a single Schechter function with parameters φ* = 2.30×10⁻³, log(M*/M⊙)=10.83, α=-1.14. Red gas-rich galaxies are 18% by number but 54% by stellar mass. Gas-rich galaxies constitute ~33% of local stellar mass density and ~39% of galaxy counts.
AI.conclusion: Gas-rich galaxies are a significant component of the local Universe, with red gas-rich galaxies being mass-dominant despite their rarity; the derived M_HI–M_star relation is free from selection bias.

title: A Multimodal Approach to Star--Galaxy Separation using SPHEREx Spectrophotometry and DESI Legacy Survey Imaging
summary: Stellar contamination is a critical systematic for increasingly precise large-scale structure analyses from ongoing and next-generation surveys. Experiments targeting constraints on local primordial non-Gaussianity with $σ(f_{\rm NL}^{\rm loc}) \sim \mathcal{O}(1)$ demand sub-percent stellar contamination rates to avoid misidentifying spurious large-scale power induced by Galactic structure as true cosmological signal. In this work, we explore the use of multimodal models for star--galaxy separation, harnessing the information from both optical broad-band imaging data and SPHEREx near-infrared low-resolution spectrophotometry. The two modalities are integrated using contrastive learning, which projects image- and spectrum-based embeddings into a shared latent space. We find that classifiers trained on these transformed representations outperform those trained on the original embeddings and show less performance degradation when simpler classifiers are used. These results suggest that multimodal alignment organizes the embedding space along dimensions that are better suited to source classification. The improvement is particularly strong for image-based classification, which we connect to increased predictability of highly-discriminative infrared spectral features from the transformed image embeddings. Applying redshift error-based selections and extrapolating to the full SPHEREx footprint, we demonstrate that stellar contamination can be controlled at the sub-percent level across most of the extragalactic sky, with completeness tradeoffs largely confined to low redshift. Our work highlights the utility of multimodal methods for modern galaxy surveys such as SPHEREx and $\textit{Rubin}$ LSST.

AI.tldr: This paper uses multimodal contrastive learning combining optical imaging and SPHEREx NIR spectrophotometry to achieve sub-percent stellar contamination for cosmological analyses targeting $\sigma(f_{\rm NL}^{\rm loc}) \sim \mathcal{O}(1)$.
AI.motivation: Stellar contamination is a critical systematic for large-scale structure analyses, particularly for constraining local primordial non-Gaussianity where sub-percent contamination rates are needed to avoid misidentifying Galactic structure signal as cosmological.
AI.method: Multimodal models using contrastive learning to align image-based (optical broadband) and spectrum-based (SPHEREx NIR low-resolution spectrophotometry) embeddings into a shared latent space, then training classifiers on these transformed representations.
AI.result: Classifiers trained on contrastively aligned embeddings outperform those on original embeddings, with less degradation for simpler classifiers. Image-based classification improves significantly due to increased predictability of infrared spectral features. Stellar contamination can be controlled at sub-percent levels across most extragalactic sky.
AI.conclusion: Multimodal contrastive learning is highly effective for star-galaxy separation in modern surveys like SPHEREx and Rubin LSST, enabling the sub-percent contamination required for precision primordial non-Gaussianity constraints.

title: High-Resolution [CI] $({^3\mathrm{P}_2}\rightarrow{^3\mathrm{P}_1})$ and CO $(J=7\rightarrow6)$ Observations of Circumnuclear Disks in Nearby Seyfert Galaxies
summary: We present [CI] $({^3\mathrm{P}_2}\mathrm{-}{^3\mathrm{P}_1})$, CO $(J=7\mathrm{-}6)$, and 800-GHz continuum observations of the circumnuclear disks (CNDs) in the Seyfert galaxies NGC 613 and NGC 1808 with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array. The images reveal the distributions of neutral gas and dust in nearby galaxy nuclei at a resolution of $0.2''$ (10 pc) which is unprecedented at these frequencies. Both lines and continuum exhibit peaks at the position of molecular tori. The maximum [CI]$({^3\mathrm{P}_2}\mathrm{-}{^3\mathrm{P}_1})/({^3\mathrm{P}_1}\mathrm{-}{^3\mathrm{P}_0})$ integrated-intensity ratio is $\approx1.1$ $(\mathrm{K~km~s}^{-1}$ scale) in the region of the torus, yielding an excitation temperature of $T_\mathrm{ex}\approx60~\mathrm{K}$ under the approximation of local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) and optically thin emission. A non-LTE radiative transfer analysis of the [CI] line ratio in the CND constrains the density and kinetic temperature of molecular gas to $n_\mathrm{H_2}>10^3~\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$ and $T_\mathrm{k}>50~\mathrm{K}$, respectively. To estimate the C/CO abundance ratio and physical conditions, we simultaneously modeled the [CI] and multiple CO lines, and obtained solutions with densities and temperatures of $n_\mathrm{H_2}\sim10^{3\mathrm{-}4}~\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$ and $T_\mathrm{k}\sim80\mathrm{-}250~\mathrm{K}$ in the central 63 pc. The C/CO ratios are $\approx2$ in NGC 613 and $\approx0.6$ in NGC 1808. C/CO tends to increase with $T_\mathrm{k}$ and decrease with $n_\mathrm{H_2}$ in the CND, which is consistent with models of photodissociation regions. Based on the kinematics of gas traced by [CI] $({^3\mathrm{P}_2}\mathrm{-}{^3\mathrm{P}_1})$ and CO $(J=7\mathrm{-}6)$, the mass of the supermassive black hole at the center of NGC 613 is estimated to be $\sim2\times10^7~M_\odot$.

AI.tldr: This paper presents ALMA observations of [CI] and CO lines and 800-GHz continuum in the circumnuclear disks of NGC 613 and NGC 1808 at ~10 pc resolution, deriving gas excitation conditions, C/CO abundance ratios, and a black hole mass estimate for NGC 613.
AI.motivation: To reveal the distribution and physical conditions of neutral gas and dust in nearby Seyfert galaxy nuclei at unprecedented high resolution (~10 pc), and to constrain the C/CO abundance ratio and black hole mass.
AI.method: ALMA observations of [CI] (³P₂–³P₁), CO (J=7–6), and 800-GHz continuum at 0.2″ resolution; LTE and non-LTE radiative transfer analysis of [CI] line ratios; simultaneous modeling of [CI] and multiple CO lines to derive C/CO, density, and kinetic temperature; kinematic modeling for black hole mass estimate.
AI.result: Maximum [CI] line ratio ~1.1 (T_ex ≈60 K under LTE); non-LTE analysis gives n_H₂ > 10³ cm⁻³ and T_k > 50 K; best-fit solutions: n_H₂ ~ 10³⁻⁴ cm⁻³, T_k ~ 80–250 K in central 63 pc; C/CO ≈ 2 (NGC 613) and ≈ 0.6 (NGC 1808); black hole mass ~2×10⁷ M⊙ for NGC 613.
AI.conclusion: C/CO increases with T_k and decreases with n_H₂, consistent with photodissociation region models; high-resolution [CI] and CO lines are effective for probing CND gas conditions and measuring black hole masses in active galaxies.

title: A lower bound on primordial power spectrum from halo substructure
summary: We investigate how the primordial curvature perturbation of a certain wavelength scale affects the halo and subhalo structure. Primordial power spectrum considered in this paper features a nearly scale-invariant form with a cutoff at the wavenumber $ k = \mathcal{O}(1)~$Mpc$^{-1}$ and an additional log-normal bump at smaller scales. We compute the host halo evolution, as well as the subhalo mass function. To be consistent with the observations of stellar streams and gravitational lensing data, the amplitude of the bump that is typically the same or larger than $10^{-9}$ of the primordial curvature perturbation should be present at the wavenumbers of $10$ - $30$ Mpc$^{-1}$.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how primordial curvature perturbations at specific wavelength scales influence halo and subhalo structure, using a power spectrum with a scale-invariant form, a cutoff at k ~ O(1) Mpc⁻¹, and an additional log-normal bump at smaller scales. To match stellar stream and gravitational lensing observations, the bump amplitude must be ≥10⁻⁹ of the primordial curvature perturbation at wavenumbers 10–30 Mpc⁻¹.
AI.motivation: To understand how primordial curvature perturbations at specific wavelength scales affect the formation and structure of dark matter halos and subhalos, and to constrain the primordial power spectrum using observational data.
AI.method: The authors consider a primordial power spectrum with a nearly scale-invariant form cut off at k ~ O(1) Mpc⁻¹ plus an additional log-normal bump at smaller scales. They compute host halo evolution and subhalo mass functions, comparing results with stellar stream and gravitational lensing observations.
AI.result: To be consistent with observations, the bump amplitude must be at least ~10⁻⁹ of the primordial curvature perturbation at wavenumbers 10–30 Mpc⁻¹.
AI.conclusion: Small-scale primordial features (log-normal bump) significantly impact subhalo structure, and observational data from stellar streams and lensing provide constraints on the amplitude and scale of such features in the primordial power spectrum.

title: ALMA CO-CAVITY II. Resolved Scaling Relations in Void Galaxies
comment: 21 pages, 14 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Scaling relations involving star formation rates (SFRs), molecular gas mass, and stellar mass are key to understand galaxy evolution, and have previously been explored at resolved scales. However, they have not been examined with particular emphasis on the large-scale environments (LSEs). In this work, we study the resolved Schmidt-Kennicutt relation (rSK), molecular gas main sequence (rMGMS) and star-forming main sequence (rSFMS) from a sample of 41 void galaxies (VGs) residing in the least dense regions of the Universe. Using high-resolution interferometric CO(1-0) data and optical IFU data from the ALMA CO-CAVITY and CAVITY surveys at scales of 2.5" (0.8-2.1 kpc), we study these relations for the full sample as well as for individual galaxies in voids. We fit the relations, finding a similar parametrisation as that used for galaxies from all LSEs. However, the rMGMS is the tightest of the three relations ($σ_{rMGMS}=0.16$ dex, $σ_{rSK}=0.21$ dex, and $σ_{rSFMS}=0.24$ dex), unlike in other samples. We find that a large source of deviations in the relations comes from galaxy-to-galaxy variations. However, the rMGMS is less affected by these variations. It has been suggested that the rMGMS arises from the concentration of molecular gas within the gravitational potential set by the stellar content and dark matter. We hypothesise that deviations from the rMGMS trace changes in the gravitational potential occurring on longer time-scales, whereas deviations in the rSK and the rSFMS are driven by more rapid variations in the SFR. This distinction is particularly relevant for our sample of VGs because the 41 ALMA CO-CAVITY VGs are more isolated than galaxies in other LSEs, and therefore are less affected by events that can significantly alter the gas distribution or trigger SF on short time-scales. In this sense, the rMGMS is likely the most stable of these relations over time.

AI.tldr: This paper studies resolved scaling relations (Schmidt-Kennicutt, molecular gas main sequence, star-forming main sequence) in 41 void galaxies, finding the rMGMS to be the tightest and most stable relation, with deviations linked to gravitational potential changes versus rapid SFR variations.
AI.motivation: Scaling relations between SFR, molecular gas, and stellar mass are well-studied at resolved scales but have not been examined with emphasis on large-scale environments, particularly void galaxies in the least dense regions of the Universe.
AI.method: Analyzed 41 void galaxies using high-resolution ALMA CO(1-0) interferometric data and optical IFU data from CAVITY surveys at 2.5" (0.8-2.1 kpc) resolution, fitting the resolved Schmidt-Kennicutt relation (rSK), molecular gas main sequence (rMGMS), and star-forming main sequence (rSFMS).
AI.result: The rMGMS is the tightest relation (σ=0.16 dex) compared to rSK (0.21 dex) and rSFMS (0.24 dex), contrary to other samples. Galaxy-to-galaxy variations are a major source of deviations, but rMGMS is least affected. The relations show similar parametrization to galaxies from all large-scale environments.
AI.conclusion: The rMGMS likely reflects the concentration of molecular gas within the gravitational potential (stellar+dark matter), with deviations tracing slow gravitational potential changes, while rSK and rSFMS deviations are driven by rapid SFR variations. Void galaxies' isolation makes the rMGMS the most stable relation over time.

title: Reviving the Affleck-Dine Curvaton Scenario with Compensated Isocurvature Perturbations
summary: We revisit the Affleck-Dine curvaton scenario in the framework of supersymmetry, taking Q-ball formation into account. In this scenario, a scalar field carrying baryon number, namely the Affleck-Dine field, generates both the curvature perturbations and the baryon asymmetry of the Universe. However, correlated baryon isocurvature perturbations are inevitably generated, resulting in excessively large correlated matter isocurvature perturbations. We propose a mechanism to suppress them, in which the correlated baryon isocurvature perturbations are canceled by anti-correlated dark matter isocurvature perturbations, thereby realizing compensated isocurvature perturbations. We show that the scenario can simultaneously account for the baryon asymmetry and the observed curvature perturbations of the Universe without generating excessively large matter isocurvature perturbations.

AI.tldr: The paper revisits the Affleck-Dine curvaton scenario in supersymmetry with Q-ball formation. It proposes a mechanism where correlated baryon isocurvature perturbations are canceled by anti-correlated dark matter isocurvature perturbations (compensated isocurvature perturbations) to avoid excessively large matter isocurvature perturbations, simultaneously accounting for baryon asymmetry and observed curvature perturbations.
AI.motivation: The Affleck-Dine curvaton scenario generates both curvature perturbations and baryon asymmetry, but inevitably produces correlated baryon isocurvature perturbations, leading to excessively large matter isocurvature perturbations that conflict with observations.
AI.method: The authors propose a compensated isocurvature perturbation mechanism where correlated baryon isocurvature perturbations are canceled by anti-correlated dark matter isocurvature perturbations, within the supersymmetric framework including Q-ball formation.
AI.result: The proposed mechanism successfully suppresses excessively large matter isocurvature perturbations while retaining the ability to generate both baryon asymmetry and curvature perturbations.
AI.conclusion: The scenario can simultaneously account for baryon asymmetry and observed curvature perturbations without generating excessively large matter isocurvature perturbations, by realizing compensated isocurvature perturbations through cancellation between baryon and dark matter components.

title: Identifying and Distinguishing Quenching Galaxies with Spatially Resolved Star Formation in the Hubble Frontier Fields
comment: 25 pages, 11 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to OJAp
summary: We investigate the nature and prevalence of different quenching signatures for 1437 galaxies with $M_{*} \geqslant 10^{8}~\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ and $\text{SFR} \geqslant 10^{-3}~M_{\odot}~\text{yr}^{-1}$ in the Hubble Frontier Fields through spatially resolved spectral energy distribution fitting with \texttt{FAST++}. We use the morphological metrics previously presented in our series of investigations to quantify the distribution of star formation, and use a $k$-nearest neighbors algorithm to classify quenching galaxies into different quenching pathways, including an inside-out pathway and an outside-in pathway. We find 129 galaxies have morphologies consistent with an inside-out quenching pathway, and 70 are consistent with an outside-in pathway. Inside-out quenching galaxies are $0.8^{+0.2}_{-0.1}~\text{dex}$ more massive compared to outside-in quenching galaxies, where both populations are more massive in clusters than the field, by $0.8^{+0.3}_{-0.1}~\text{dex}$. Inside-out quenching galaxies are found more often in clusters (106/129), compared to outside-in quenching galaxies (25/70). In clusters, the fraction of inside-out quenching galaxies strongly increases with mass, representing ${\sim}$30% of the non-quenched galaxy population at high masses. A milder evolution is seen in the field. The fraction of outside-in quenching galaxies is independent of mass, representing ${\lesssim}$10% of the non-quenched population, in both the cluster and field. We find no strong dependence for the fraction of any population with estimated infall time, except massive inside-out quenching galaxies, which increase in fraction with increasing infall time.

AI.tldr: Study of 1,437 galaxies in Hubble Frontier Fields reveals 129 inside-out quenching galaxies (more massive, cluster-dominated) and 70 outside-in quenching galaxies, with inside-out quenching increasing with mass and infall time while outside-in quenching remains ~10% regardless of environment.
AI.motivation: To investigate the nature and prevalence of different quenching signatures (inside-out vs. outside-in) in galaxies across different environments (cluster vs. field) using spatially resolved data.
AI.method: Spatially resolved SED fitting with FAST++ on 1,437 galaxies (M* ≥ 10^8 M☉, SFR ≥ 10^-3 M☉/yr) in Hubble Frontier Fields; used morphological metrics and k-nearest neighbors algorithm to classify quenching pathways.
AI.result: 129 inside-out quenching galaxies (0.8 dex more massive than outside-in); 70 outside-in quenching galaxies. Inside-out galaxies are more common in clusters (106/129) vs. outside-in (25/70). Inside-out fraction increases with mass (~30% at high masses in clusters) and infall time; outside-in fraction is mass-independent (~10%) in both environments.
AI.conclusion: Inside-out and outside-in quenching represent distinct pathways with different environmental and mass dependencies: inside-out quenching is strongly linked to cluster environment and mass, while outside-in quenching is largely independent of these factors.

title: Inferences for f(R) Models from Late-Time Megamaser Observational Data
summary: In this work, we study three widely used models of f(R) gravity, namely HuSawicki, Starobinsky and ArcTanh along with the standard cosmology model ($Λ$CDM). For this, we employ the megamaser angular diameter distance and velocity measurements from the Megamaser Cosmology Project, which provide a purely geometric determination of the Hubble constant. We constrain the parameters using the Markov Chain Monte Carlo method. Our results show that values of the Hubble Constant, $H_{0}$, obtained for all four models are in concordance with its value obtained from other late-time observational data such as SNe Ia. The constraints on $H_{0}$ in all the models under study are restrictive and the marginalized estimates lie close to 73 $\mathrm {km s^{-1} Mpc^{-1}}$. The marginalized estimates of the deviation parameter, b, for the three f(R) gravity models lie close to zero. This late-time dataset, thus predicts that f(R) models mimic $Λ$CDM. However, the matter density, $Ω_m$, remains weakly constrained for all the models with its marginalized estimate close to 0.5. Further, comparison of the four models (f(R) models and $Λ$CDM) using information criteria such as Akaike Information Criterion and Bayesian Information Criterion shows that within current uncertainties, the dataset finds f(R) models statistically indistinguishable from $Λ$CDM. This is consistent with the fact that the favoured value of b for each of the f(R) models lies close to zero.

AI.tldr: This paper constrains f(R) gravity models (HuSawicki, Starobinsky, ArcTanh) and ΛCDM using megamaser angular diameter distance and velocity data from the Megamaser Cosmology Project. Using MCMC, they find H₀ ≈ 73 km/s/Mpc for all models, the deviation parameter b is near zero for f(R) models (indicating they mimic ΛCDM), while Ωₘ (~0.5) remains weakly constrained. Information criteria show f(R) models are statistically indistinguishable from ΛCDM.
AI.motivation: To test whether f(R) gravity models can be distinguished from ΛCDM using purely geometric megamaser distance measurements, and to obtain independent constraints on H₀ from late-time data.
